says: A socket's close in next/ runs `p.leave`, then `p.disconnect`, then drops the connection from its map, in one sequence, so any failure or defect in leave skips the disconnect and leaves the closed socket's entry in the map.
proof: On this branch before its fix, with a log line added at each step, `vitest run --project next-visual next/apps/fabrika/e2e/client-protocol.visual.test.ts -t "headless client's tile says Ended"` printed `DIAG leave gateways done` and then `DIAG from cause Cause([Die(NoSuchElementError)])` inside Project.leave; nothing after it in the close ran, since `rpc(p.disconnect(...))` and `connections.delete(ws)` follow `rpc(p.leave(...))` at lines 195 to 197.
cost: One defect in leave also keeps the door's client row and the in-memory connection alive for a socket that is gone, so a later fault in leave spreads into presence and memory with no sign.
